liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the Iko Iko into Beat It On Down The Line opener awesome; Weir takes a verse in Iko Iko, which prompts Jerry to talk about 'Hey Now' [2][23]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 other source): The band gives a twenty count intro for Beat It On Down The Line [2]
- **Althea** (1 review): Althea is described as nice, and Box of Rain as great [23]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Playing In The Band into Franklin's Tower, Miracle, then Playing jam is singled out as a very good stretch [23]
- **Playin' Jam** (1 review): The Playin' jam before drums flirts with Supplication [26]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (1 review): Dear Mr. Fantasy was the high point of the second set [24]
- Bobby was especially energetic and worked hard this night [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **encore call**: rare: 13 archived performances [34]
- Earliest performances in the archive: We Want Phil [34]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-03-28.senn.koucky.gmb.32520.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 129 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1986-03-28.156133.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 21 songs; 124 min [5]. Said about its sound: Low-frequency and bass distortion throughout the set, from overloaded preamps or weak batteries [5]
- **gd1986-03-28.166964.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 127 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [7]
- **gd1986-03-28.aud.alexander.tetzeli.79289.flac16**: audience recording; 19 songs; 128 min [8]
- **gd86-03-28.neumann-hogan.hogan.5004.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 116 min; rated 4/5 by 11 [17]. Said about its sound: The audience recording is decent, not bad [22]
- **gd1986-03-28.fob.thompson.motb.88950.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 123 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [18]. Said about its sound: This Mouth of the Beast release sounds nearly like a matrix recording [33]

## Around the show

- Attendees all spotted a huge fake gorilla atop a building over a parking lot and howled [24]
- Second-set songs seem to emerge abruptly, with unclear transitions [26]
- It was a beautiful spring day in Portland, and the scene around the venue was memorable [28]
- Small arena, general admission show; tapers were allowed to set up in front of the board [1]
- A 'We want Phil' chant came before Box of Rain, and Phil answered 'Here I is folk' [2]
- A grinding PA sound, thought to be Weir's rig, appears whenever the band plays throughout this spring tour [5]
- Reviewer can't decide whether this show or Providence a few nights later was better [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-03-28.senn.koucky.gmb.32520.flac16**: taped by Bill Koucky; transferred by Bill Koucky and Chris Ladner; source: FOB Sennheiser ME88 > D5 > Maxell Metal Cassette master [1]
- **gd1986-03-28.156133.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew; Mike Davis, Kyle Holbrook, Tom Pinney, John Hance, Kenny Davis, Sean Murtha; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Source: MAUD CA Microphones: AKG c422 crossed figure 8's (X-Y at 90') head level|AKG B18 Recorder: Sony TC-D5M| Maxell MX 90's no Dolby (2nd in line) Location:… [5]. Also: Source taken with AKG C422 microphones, front of board audience recording [5]
- **gd1986-03-28.166964.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [7]
- **gd1986-03-28.aud.alexander.tetzeli.79289.flac16**: taped by Tim Alexander; transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Sennheiser 421s + Nakamichi 300s > Yamaha mixer > Sony D5 (Dolby B) > MAC [8]. Also: Audience recording by Alexander/Tetzeli; Me & My Uncle and Mexicali Blues share track 6 because they weren't tracked separately [31]
- **gd86-03-28.neumann-hogan.hogan.5004.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB (Center)> AUD> MC> CDR Neumann U87's> Uher CR240> Maxell XLII 90 Cass. Master> Marantz Pro CDR 500 [17]
- **gd1986-03-28.fob.thompson.motb.88950.flac16**: taped by D. Thompson; transferred by A. Egert and D. McCabe; source: 2 x AKG C 460 B-ULS/CK 61-ULS => Uher CR-240 >> MAC (Denon MD8 90) [18]

1986-03-28 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia

claims.text: Bobby was especially energetic and worked hard this night
The audience recording is decent, not bad
Reviewer calls the Iko Iko into Beat It On Down The Line opener awesome
Playing In The Band into Franklin's Tower, Miracle, then Playing jam is singled out as a very good stretch
Althea is described as nice, and Box of Rain as great
Attendees all spotted a huge fake gorilla atop a building over a parking lot and howled
Dear Mr. Fantasy was the high point of the second set
Reviewer can't decide whether this show or Providence a few nights later was better
The Playin' jam before drums flirts with Supplication
Second-set songs seem to emerge abruptly, with unclear transitions
It was a beautiful spring day in Portland, and the scene around the venue was memorable
Audience recording by Alexander/Tetzeli; Me & My Uncle and Mexicali Blues share track 6 because they weren't tracked separately
This Mouth of the Beast release sounds nearly like a matrix recording
Small arena, general admission show; tapers were allowed to set up in front of the board
Weir takes a verse in Iko Iko, which prompts Jerry to talk about 'Hey Now'

claims.song: Beat It On Down The Line
claims.text: The band gives a twenty count intro for Beat It On Down The Line
A 'We want Phil' chant came before Box of Rain, and Phil answered 'Here I is folk'
Low-frequency and bass distortion throughout the set, from overloaded preamps or weak batteries
A grinding PA sound, thought to be Weir's rig, appears whenever the band plays throughout this spring tour
Source taken with AKG C422 microphones, front of board audience recording
Beyer M160 master cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller
